---
title: "Practical work and communication"
---

This page describes the proposed scope. It is not a laboratory protocol or
an instruction to begin an experiment.

## Anatomy and histology

Observe representative normal tissues and organs, recognise characteristic
features and explain how structure supports function. Retain comparisons
between animal groups and the established specimen sessions.

## Physiological experiments

Carry out the course's established animal and plant experiments. Identify
the question, experimental unit, controls, measurements and units before
interpreting results. Preserve observations and distinguish variation among
organisms from repeated measurements of one organism.

The practical manual, equipment, specimen list and timetable will determine
the experiments. No new experiment is specified by this outline.

## Scientific reporting

A report should connect the physiological question, methods, results and
interpretation. Explain figures, uncertainty and limitations rather than
presenting numbers alone. Software requirements will follow the actual
practical instructions; this proposal requires no R component.

## Literature and presentation

Read scientific evidence critically, discuss physiological mechanisms and
communicate a reasoned interpretation orally and in writing. Plant
biotechnology discussion includes potential benefits, risks and ethics.
